correctness.rationale: Strict growth of \(\rho_t\) follows from \(t-(t+1)b+b^{t+1}>0\). The gate factors as \((b-1)^2P_t(b)>0\); \(P_t\) has one positive root by Descartes' rule and endpoint signs place it in \((3/5,1)\). The root asymptotic follows from the exact displacement identity.

value.rationale: RAdam was designed to remove a separate warmup-length hyperparameter by tying the transition to second-moment decay. The exact phase diagram quantifies that central design feature, explains the four unadapted updates at common defaults, and shows why the phase length becomes arbitrarily large near the method's own beta2 = 0.6 degeneracy boundary.
